Use, Principal. The principal purpose for which a lot or the principal building thereon is designed, arranged or intended, and for which it is or may be used, occupied or maintained.

Utility. Public or private water or sewer systems, water or sewer pump stations, electric power lines, fuel pipelines, telephone lines, roads, driveways, bridges, river/lake access facilities, stormwater systems, railroads, and all equipment and structures necessary to provide such services for utilities licensed or authorized to serve Newborn.

Wetlands. Areas inundated or saturated by surface or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and that under normal circumstances do support, a prévalence of vegetation typically adapted for life in saturated soil conditions. Wetlands generally include swamps, marshes, bogs and similar areas. (33 CFR 32.93) The ecological parameters for designating wetlands include hydric soils; hydrophytic vegetation, and hydrological conditions that involve a temporary or permanent source of water to cause soil saturation. Freshwater wetlands do not include any areas defined as “coastal marshlands” by the State Coastal Marshlands Protection Act.

Yard. A space on the same lot with a principal building, being open, unoccupied and unobstructed by buildings or structures from ground to sky except where encroachments and accessory buildings are expressly permitted.

Yard, Front. An unoccupied yard extending the full width of the lot and situated between the right-of-way line and the front line of building projected to the side lines of that lot. The depth shall be measured between the front line of the building projected to the side lines of the lot and the right-of-way line. Covered porches, enclosed or unenclosed, shall be considered as part of the principal building and shall not project into a required front yard.

Yard, Rear. A yard of the full width of the lot and between the rear line of the lot and the rear line of the principal building projected to the side lines. On corner lots the rear yard is at the opposite side of the lot from the front yard.

Yard, Side. A yard between the side line of the building and the adjacent side line of the lot from rear line of front yard to front line of rear yard. If no front yard is required, the rear boundary of the side yard shall be the rear line.
